 KEY TAKEAWAYS:
 Nepal's collapse against India A in Doha was among the most dramatic in cricket.
 A strict ICC rule decides which record books this shocking result can enter.
 Cricket News  explains why this result will not be counted as an official ODI. 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement MORE:  India A vs Nepal ACC Men's Asia Cup Rising Stars result, highlights & score as Nepal collapse for 26 in Doha 
 Why does Nepal's 26 all out against India A not count as the lowest score in ODI cricket history? ICC List A rules explained
 Nepal were bowled out for 26 by India A, and the number was low enough to send cricket fans straight to the record books. The score came in Match 4 of Group B at the DP World ACC Men's Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026, a 50-over tournament being played in Doha.
 Nepal won the toss and chose to bowl first, a decision that looked sound at the start but proved costly as the day went on.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement India A made full use of the batting conditions and finished their innings on 332/9 in 50 overs. Kumar Kushagra top-scored with 117 off 102 balls, with ten fours and five sixes, while captain Tilak Varma made 107. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi chipped in with 26, and Lalit Rajbanshi and Sandeep Lamichhane took three wickets apiece for Nepal.
 The chase was over almost before it began, as Nepal lasted only 11.3 overs and lost by 306 runs. They were 1/4 after just two overs and 17/7 by the 8.1-over mark. Not one of their batters reached double figures. 
 Prince Yadav led the attack with five wickets, and Harshit Rana backed him up with four. Shahbaz Ahmed picked up the last wicket to wrap up the innings at 26. The margin of victory, 306 runs, is the eighth-largest by runs in List A history.
 Yet, Nepal's 26 all out is not the lowest ODI total ever. The reason comes down to how the International Cricket Council classifies matches. Even though this was a 50-over game and Nepal's senior national side, which has official ODI status, was playing, India fielded India A and not their main team. That difference matters a great deal.
 Under Section 2 of the ICC's Classification of Official Cricket, a 50-over game becomes an official ODI only when both teams are senior national sides with ODI status.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Matches involving an 'A' team or age-group team shall not be classified as ODI matches. As a result, the match can't be recorded as an ODI. It does, however, count as an official List A game, because Nepal hold ODI status and India A is the second-string side of a Full Member nation.
 What counts as an official ODI? A simple guide to ICC match classification
 A match gets ODI status in three situations. The first is when two senior Full Member teams meet, such as India and Australia. The second is when a senior Full Member side plays one of the eight Associate Members with men's ODI status, which are Canada, Namibia, Nepal, Oman, Scotland, the Netherlands, the UAE and the USA. The third is when two of those Associate teams play each other.

 Lowest ODI totals in history: Zimbabwe and the USA still hold the record at 35
 Since Nepal's score doesn't count, the official record for the lowest men's ODI total remains with two teams. Zimbabwe made 35 against Sri Lanka in Harare in 2004, and the USA were dismissed for the same score against Nepal in Kirtipur in 2020.
